Pairs with baltia_jfk_ground_truth.json (37 obligations) and baltia_jfk_telemetry.json (mock actuals).
PRIMARY tracking surface = SUPPLIER (Swissport) obligations -- the 12 KPIs in this contract
explicitly tagged party_role='supplier' (Swissport is the party bound by the commitment):
manning/staffing, conditional-charge rules (technical landing, ramp return, night/Sunday/
holiday surcharge ban), liability cap, statutory pass-through, CPI escalation floor, and the
3 Annex A scope-of-service references. These are grouped into one dedicated source
(supplier_obligations_log) so connecting it is the demo's headline moment.
SECONDARY = CUSTOMER (Baltia) obligations -- 10 fee-schedule / notice / schedule-adherence
KPIs tagged party_role='customer', tracked across 4 smaller sources as a compliance baseline.
22 of 37 obligations tracked; the remaining 15 are extracted but unmapped (tiered labor
rates, contract-term/administrative clauses, reference-only items without a clean single
4 breaches total: 3 supplier (75%) + 1 customer (25%), matching the pitch's primary focus.
_breach_summary_notes: Each row is one occurrence (evidence record), not one KPI -- mirrors how the real breach engine
writes one contract_kpi_breaches doc per evaluate_kpi call. A KPI with recurring violations
(006, 010, 011, 032) appears multiple times; each amount is fully traceable to its evidence_record_id
in baltia_jfk_telemetry.json. GHA-032 is billed as ONE audit finding (not 254 line items) because
that mirrors how a real rate-card escalation audit is actually delivered to a Recoveries team --
an aggregate reconciliation against the Swissport monthly billing summaries, not per-turnaround rows.
